A list of sort objects that specifies how the records will be ordered.
Each sort object must have a fieldId key specifying the field to sort on (ID or name), and an optional direction key that is either "asc" or "desc".
The default direction is "asc".
Records are sorted by the first sort object first, then by the second sort object for records that have the same value for the first sort, and so on.
Example sort by a single field in descending order: [{"fieldId": "Status", "direction": "desc"}]
Example sort by two fields, first ascending then descending: [{"fieldId": "Priority", "direction": "asc"}, {"fieldId": "Created", "direction": "desc"}]

operator.description:
The operator to use to combine the operands (filter conditions).
Acceptable values are 'and' and 'or'.
The default operator is 'and'.

The comparison operator for this filter condition, applied to the operands.
Acceptable values are =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isWithin, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, contains, doesNotContain, filename, fileType, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
For singleSelect and singleCollaborator fields, use =, !=, isAnyOf, or isNoneOf.
For multipleSelects and multipleCollaborators fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, or doesNotContain.

matchGroupsByMembership.description:
Only set this when operand is a collaborator field.
When true, groups are matched by their individual members.
When false, groups are matched by their literal group ID.

operands.description:
The operands (arguments) to the comparison operator.
The first operand must be a field ID. Example: "fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM". Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
The second operand depends on the operator and field type:
    - isEmpty, isNotEmpty: No second operand (use a single-element array with just the field ID).
    - =, !=, contains, doesNotContain: A string for text fields, a number for number fields, a boolean for checkbox fields.
    - <, >, <=, >=: A number.
    - For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields: The second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selABCDEFGHIJKLM") obtained from get_table_schema, not the choice
    name.
    - hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, doesNotContain: An array of strings (e.g., choice IDs for select fields, collaborator IDs for collaborator fields).
    - For date/datetime fields with =, !=, <, >, <=, >=: The second operand is a date value object, e.g. {"mode": "today", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "exactDate",
    "exactDate": "2024-01-15", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, or {"mode": "daysAgo", "numberOfDays": 7, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - isWithin (date fields only): The second operand is a date range object, e.g. {"mode": "pastWeek", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "pastNumberOfDays", "numberOfDays":
    30, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - filename: A string to match against attachment filenames.
    - fileType: Either "image" or "text".
For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, the second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selet1KAKDTOhXQJk") obtained from get_table_schema.

A list of filter conditions to apply to the records. These are combined using the top-level operator (default "and").
Each filter condition must have an "operator" key (the comparison operator, e.g. "=", "contains", "isEmpty", etc) and an "operands" key (an array where
the first element is a field ID and the optional second element is the value to compare against).
Example: [{"operator": "contains", "operands": ["fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM", "apple"]}]

tool.description:
Creates new records in an Airtable table.

By default the response includes only the fields you wrote. To also include fields you did not write (e.g. the primary field or formula results), pass their IDs in fieldIds.
You can create up to 50 records per request. To create more than 50 records, make multiple requests.

{"baseId": "appZfrNIUEip5MazD", "tableId": "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG", "records": [{"fields": {"fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV": "Launch meeting", "fldulcCPDVz87Bmnw": 42, "fld8WsrpLHHevsnW8": "In progress", "fldgD18XtsueoiguT": ["Urgent", "Q1"]}}]}

fields.description:

numbers for numeric fields, arrays of strings for multipleSelects fields).

For multipleSelects fields, use an array of option name strings (e.g., ["Tag1", "Tag2"]).

color.description: Rating color. Use "yellowBright" for a standard rating.

icon.description: Rating icon. Use "star" for a standard rating.

name.description: Field names must be unique within the table (case-insensitive).

linkedTableId.description: The ID of the table to link to. Use list_tables_for_base to get the table ID.

name.description: Field names must be unique within the table (case-insensitive).

formula.description: The formula expression. Reference fields by name ({Field Name}) or ID ({fldXXXXXXXXXXXXXX}). Use get_table_schema to discover available field names.

name.description: Field names must be unique within the table (case-insensitive).

baseId.description:
The ID of the base containing the table.

Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.

tool.name: airtable.update_field
tool.title: update_field
tool.description:
Updates the name, description, and/or options of a field in an existing Airtable table.
At least one of name, description, or options must be specified.
To get baseId and tableId, use the search_bases and list_tables_for_base tools first.
To get the fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.
Example: update a field's name and description:
{"baseId": "appZfrNIUEip5MazD", "tableId": "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG", "fieldId": "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV", "name": "Updated Name", "description": "Updated description"}
Example: update a formula field's expression:
{"baseId": "appZfrNIUEip5MazD", "tableId": "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG", "fieldId": "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV", "options": {"formula": "{Quantity} * {Price}"}}

fieldId.description:
The ID of the field to update.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

name.description: The new name for the field. Must be unique within the table (case-insensitive).

formula.description: The new formula expression (formula fields only). Reference fields by name ({Field Name}) or ID ({fldXXXXXXXXXXXXXX}).

baseId.description:
The ID of the base containing the table.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

tableId.description:
The ID of the table containing the field.
Must start with "tbl" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG".
Do not substitute user-facing names for tableId.
To get tableId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

tool.name: airtable.display_records_for_table
tool.title: display_records_for_table
tool.description:
Displays an interactive widget showing record data queried from an Airtable table.
Do not assume baseId and tableId. Obtain these from search_bases → list_tables_for_base.
Do not attempt to pass filterByFormula. Look carefully at the filters parameter.
Pre-requisite: If filtering on singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, you must call get_table_schema first to get the choice IDs.
Aim to provide 6 to 10 relevant fields via the 'fieldIds' parameter.
The possible view types are kanban and list.
Set viewType to kanban when there is a singleSelect field that is requested.
Aim to provide at least 1 sort when there is a reasonable column to sort by.
Note: singleSelect and multipleSelects field values are returned as objects (e.g., {"id": "sel...", "name": "Option", "color": "blue"}) or arrays of such objects. When writing these values back via create_records_for_table or update_records_for_table, use the plain string name (e.g., "Option") instead of the object.

cursor.description:
The cursor to start from. To begin from the first record, do not include a cursor.
For a subsequent paginated request, include the nextCursor from the previous response.

pageSize.description:
The maximum number of records to return in the response.
The server may respond with fewer records than this value when the total set has fewer records than this value.
Defaults to 1000.

stackingFieldId.description:
The ID of the field to stack the data by. Only used when viewType is kanban.
This field must be a single select field.
If no logical single select field exists, then do not set this parameter.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

fieldId.description: The field to sort by. Accepts either a field ID (e.g., "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV") or field name (e.g., "Status").

sort.description:
A list of sort objects that specifies how the records will be ordered.
Each sort object must have a fieldId key specifying the field to sort on (ID or name), and an optional direction key that is either "asc" or "desc".
The default direction is "asc".
Records are sorted by the first sort object first, then by the second sort object for records that have the same value for the first sort, and so on.
Example sort by a single field in descending order: [{"fieldId": "Status", "direction": "desc"}]
Example sort by two fields, first ascending then descending: [{"fieldId": "Priority", "direction": "asc"}, {"fieldId": "Created", "direction": "desc"}]

operator.description:
The operator to use to combine the operands (filter conditions).
Acceptable values are 'and' and 'or'.
The default operator is 'and'.

The comparison operator for this filter condition, applied to the operands.
Acceptable values are =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isWithin, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, contains, doesNotContain, filename, fileType, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
For singleSelect and singleCollaborator fields, use =, !=, isAnyOf, or isNoneOf.
For multipleSelects and multipleCollaborators fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, or doesNotContain.

matchGroupsByMembership.description:
Only set this when operand is a collaborator field.
When true, groups are matched by their individual members.
When false, groups are matched by their literal group ID.

operands.description:
The operands (arguments) to the comparison operator.
The first operand must be a field ID. Example: "fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM". Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
The second operand depends on the operator and field type:
    - isEmpty, isNotEmpty: No second operand (use a single-element array with just the field ID).
    - =, !=, contains, doesNotContain: A string for text fields, a number for number fields, a boolean for checkbox fields.
    - <, >, <=, >=: A number.
    - For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields: The second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selABCDEFGHIJKLM") obtained from get_table_schema, not the choice
    name.
    - hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, doesNotContain: An array of strings (e.g., choice IDs for select fields, collaborator IDs for collaborator fields).
    - For date/datetime fields with =, !=, <, >, <=, >=: The second operand is a date value object, e.g. {"mode": "today", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "exactDate",
    "exactDate": "2024-01-15", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, or {"mode": "daysAgo", "numberOfDays": 7, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - isWithin (date fields only): The second operand is a date range object, e.g. {"mode": "pastWeek", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "pastNumberOfDays", "numberOfDays":
    30, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - filename: A string to match against attachment filenames.
    - fileType: Either "image" or "text".
For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, the second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selet1KAKDTOhXQJk") obtained from get_table_schema.

A list of filter conditions to apply to the records. These are combined using the top-level operator (default "and").
Each filter condition must have an "operator" key (the comparison operator, e.g. "=", "contains", "isEmpty", etc) and an "operands" key (an array where
the first element is a field ID and the optional second element is the value to compare against).
Example: [{"operator": "contains", "operands": ["fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM", "apple"]}]

coverImageFieldId.description:
The ID of the field to use as the cover image. Only used when viewType is kanban.
This field must be an attachment field. Prefer fields that seem to contain
images rather than documents or other file types.
If no logical attachment field exists, then do not set this parameter.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

baseId.description:
The ID of the base containing the table.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

viewType.description:
Type of view to display the data in.

Potential values in order of preference:
- kanban: displays the data in a visual kanban board, e.g. when asked to show the status of tasks.
- list: displays the data in a basic list.

tableId.description:
The table to list records from.
Accepts either a table ID (e.g., "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG") or a table name (e.g., "Orders").
Names are resolved case-insensitively within the base.
To discover tables, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

fieldIds.description:
Only data for fields whose IDs are in this list will be included in the result.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

recordIds.description:
An array of record IDs to filter by. Only records with these IDs will be returned.
Must start with "rec" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "recZOTa3BDHxlJNzf".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs
To get recordId, use the list_records_for_table tool or display_records_for_table tools.

tool.name: airtable.list_records_for_page
tool.title: list_records_for_page
tool.description:
Lists records from an interface page. Pages may display data from one table (simple pages)
or multiple related tables (hierarchy pages, e.g. projects → tasks).

The response contains recordsByTableId, a map from table ID to the records from that table.
For simple pages this has one entry; for hierarchy pages it has one entry per configured level.
Use the table IDs from list_pages_for_base to identify which table is which.

Use this for bases with permissionLevel "none" (interface-only access), or when the user asks about interface/page data.
Obtain pageId from list_pages_for_base.

The default operator is 'and'.

Acceptable values are =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isWithin, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, contains, doesNotContain, filename, fileType, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
For singleSelect and singleCollaborator fields, use =, !=, isAnyOf, or isNoneOf.
For multipleSelects and multipleCollaborators fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, or doesNotContain.

matchGroupsByMembership.description:
Only set this when operand is a collaborator field.
When true, groups are matched by their individual members.
When false, groups are matched by their literal group ID.

operands.description:
The operands (arguments) to the comparison operator.
The first operand must be a field ID. Example: "fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM". Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
The second operand depends on the operator and field type:
    - isEmpty, isNotEmpty: No second operand (use a single-element array with just the field ID).
    - =, !=, contains, doesNotContain: A string for text fields, a number for number fields, a boolean for checkbox fields.
    - <, >, <=, >=: A number.
    - For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields: The second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selABCDEFGHIJKLM") obtained from get_table_schema, not the choice
    name.
    - hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, doesNotContain: An array of strings (e.g., choice IDs for select fields, collaborator IDs for collaborator fields).
    - For date/datetime fields with =, !=, <, >, <=, >=: The second operand is a date value object, e.g. {"mode": "today", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "exactDate",
    "exactDate": "2024-01-15", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, or {"mode": "daysAgo", "numberOfDays": 7, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - isWithin (date fields only): The second operand is a date range object, e.g. {"mode": "pastWeek", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "pastNumberOfDays", "numberOfDays":
    30, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - filename: A string to match against attachment filenames.
    - fileType: Either "image" or "text".
For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, the second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selet1KAKDTOhXQJk") obtained from get_table_schema.

A list of filter conditions to apply to the records. These are combined using the top-level operator (default "and").
Each filter condition must have an "operator" key (the comparison operator, e.g. "=", "contains", "isEmpty", etc) and an "operands" key (an array where
the first element is a field ID and the optional second element is the value to compare against).
Example: [{"operator": "contains", "operands": ["fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM", "apple"]}]

pageId.description:
The ID of the interface page to read records from.
Must start with "pag" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "pagXxYyZzAaBbCcDd".

elementId.description:
The ID of a specific element to query records for.
Required for dashboard pages. Obtain element IDs from the dashboardElements
array in the list_pages_for_base response.
Must start with "pel" and is 17 characters long.

baseId.description:
The ID of the base (application) containing the page.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

The maximum number of records to return in the response.
The server may respond with fewer records than this value when the total set has fewer records than this value.

fieldIds.description:
Only data for fields whose IDs are in this list will be included in the result.
Pass in only the fields most useful for the user to see.
If not provided, the fields visible in the page element's visualization will be returned.
For hierarchy pages, field IDs are matched against each table — a field belonging to
the projects table will filter the projects records, and one belonging to the tasks
table will filter the tasks records. You can mix field IDs from different tables.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

navigationTargets.description:
Linked record fields on the listed records that can be expanded into detail pages.
Use get_record_for_page to navigate into a linked record's detail page.

recordsByTableId.description:

contains one entry. For hierarchy pages, each configured level has its own entry.

tool.name: airtable.list_pages_for_base
tool.title: list_pages_for_base
tool.description:
Lists all interfaces and their pages for a base.
Returns metadata about each interface and the pages within it, including page IDs, names,
and page-type-specific fields describing the page's data model or content.

Pages have a pageType: "list" pages support listing records directly,
"dashboard" pages contain visualization elements (charts, big numbers, etc.)
that aggregate data from source tables, and "overview" pages contain static authored
content (text, links) with no record data.

For record list pages, use sourceTableId and tablesByTableId to understand the data model.
For dashboard pages, use dashboardElements to understand what each element visualizes.
Each element's config describes the aggregation (e.g., a BigNumber with summaryFunction "sum"
means "sum the values of the referenced field"). To compute these values, call
list_records_for_page with the element's id as elementId to fetch
the underlying records, then aggregate them according to the config.
Overview pages are not backed by record data and cannot be used with
list_records_for_page; read their content field directly.

Use this when the user asks about interfaces, pages, or dashboards, or when a base has permissionLevel "none" (interface-only access).
Do not assume baseId. Obtain it from search_bases or list_bases.
{"baseId": "appZfrNIUEip5MazD"}

baseId.description:
The ID of the base to list pages from.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

interfaceId.description: The ID of the interface containing this page.

name.description: The name of the page.

tablesByTableId.description:
All tables on this page, keyed by table ID. For simple list pages this has one entry.
For hierarchy pages, this has one entry per configured level.
For dashboard pages, this has one entry per source table across all dashboard groups.

The table this page queries against. On hierarchy pages with multiple tables
in tablesByTableId, this identifies whichtable filters passed to
list_records_for_page will apply to.

The ID of this dashboard element. Pass this as elementId to
list_records_for_page to fetch the underlying records.

groupFieldId.description: Optional grouping field for stacked/grouped charts.

A pivot table groups records into rows by rowDimension and (optionally) cross-tabulates
into columns by columnDimension, computing one aggregated value per cell via summary.
With no columnDimension, it collapses to a single summary column per row group.

columnDimension.description: The column dimension — records are further cross-tabulated into columns by this field's values. Null means no column grouping (single summary column).

dateBucketUnit.description: Date bucketing unit. Null if not a date field.

fieldId.description: The field used for this dimension.

dateBucketUnit.description: Date bucketing unit. Null if not a date field.

Describes each visualization element on the dashboard,
including its type, configuration, and the elementId needed to fetch its underlying records.

name.description: The name of the page.

tool.name: airtable.get_record_for_page
tool.title: get_record_for_page
tool.description:
Gets a single record's details from an interface page element.
Takes a navigation path with a root record and edges representing linked record relationships.
With no edges, returns the root record. With edges, returns the last edge's linkedRecordId.
For each edge, fieldId is the linked record field to follow, and linkedRecordId is the record it points to.

Example: record A on page P has linked record field F pointing to record B.
- Fetch A: path = {root: {pageId: P, recordId: A}, edges: []}
- Fetch B: path = {root: {pageId: P, recordId: A}, edges: [{fieldId: F, linkedRecordId: B}]}
Each subsequent call appends to the same path without changing root.

For dashboard pages, include elementId in the root to identify the dashboard element.
Obtain element IDs from the dashboardElements array in the list_pages_for_base response.

The response includes navigationTargets listing which fieldIds can be expanded further.
To navigate deeper, append a new edge.

Requires baseId and path.
Use this for bases with permissionLevel "none" (interface-only access), or when the user asks about interface/page data.
Obtain pageId from list_pages_for_base.
Do not assume baseId. Obtain it from search_bases or list_bases

path.description:
The navigation path from the page where the record was listed.
Construct the root from the same pageId used in list_records_for_page.

linkedRecordId.description:
The record to navigate to by following the linked record field.
Must start with "rec" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "recZOTa3BDHxlJNzf".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs
To get recordId, use the list_records_for_table tool or display_records_for_table tools.

fieldId.description:
The linked record field used to traverse to the detail page.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

edges.description:
Linked record traversals leading to the target record.
Empty array if the record is directly listed on the root page.

root.description:
The page and starting record. Set once from list_records_for_page results;
stays the same as edges are appended.

pageId.description:
The page where the record was listed.
Must start with "pag" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "pagXxYyZzAaBbCcDd".

recordId.description:
A record from list_records_for_page results. With no edges, this is
the record returned. With edges, this is the starting point of the navigation.
Must start with "rec" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "recZOTa3BDHxlJNzf".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs
To get recordId, use the list_records_for_table tool or display_records_for_table tools.

elementId.description:
The ID of the dashboard element to query. Required for dashboard pages.
Obtain element IDs from the dashboardElements array in the
list_pages_for_base response.
Must start with "pel" and is 17 characters long.

interfaceId.description:
The ID of the interface that contains the page.
Must start with "pbd" and is 17 characters long.

baseId.description:
The ID of the base (application) containing the page.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

fieldIds.description:
Only data for fields whose IDs are in this list will be included in the result.
If not provided, all fields visible on the page will be returned.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

navigationTargets.description:
Linked record fields on the fetched record that can be expanded into detail pages.
To navigate, call this tool again with a new edge appended to the path:
{ fieldId: <one of these IDs>, linkedRecordId: <ID of the linked record> }.

createdTime.description: The time the record was created.

cellValuesByFieldId.description: The cell values of the record by field ID.

tool.name: airtable.search_records
tool.title: search_records
tool.description:
Searches for records in a table using a free-text query. Uses an optimized full-text index that supports fuzzy matching (handles typos) and token-based search (matches individual words regardless of order).
Call list_tables_for_base first to discover available tables and fields if needed.
Prefer this over list_records_for_table when performing free-text search on large tables. Use list_records_for_table instead when filtering by exact field values or structured filters. Not all field types are searchable. Date, rating, checkbox, and button fields are not indexed. Formula, rollup, and lookup fields are only searchable if their result type is searchable. If you need to query by unsearchable field types, use list_records_for_table with filters instead.

table.description: The table to search. Accepts either a table ID (e.g., "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG") or a table name (e.g., "Orders"). Names are resolved case-insensitively within the base.

query.description: The search query. Matches are case-insensitive and term-order independent. Examples: "acme" matches "Acme Corp", "john smith" matches "Smith, John", ""Q1 Report"" (quoted) matches the exact phrase only.

fields.description: The fields to search over. Either pass an array of field IDs/names, or the literal string "ALL_SEARCHABLE_FIELDS" to search across all searchable fields in the table. Field IDs look like "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV". Field names (e.g., "Status") are resolved case-insensitively. Note: Not all field types are searchable. If this fails, fallback to using the list_records_for_table tool instead.

baseId.description:
The ID of the base containing the table.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

tool.name: lovable.get_me
tool.title: get_me
tool.description: Get the authenticated user's profile and workspaces

tool.name: lovable.list_workspaces
tool.title: list_workspaces
tool.description: List all workspaces the user belongs to. Returns a concise summary; use get_workspace for full details. Call this first to discover workspace IDs, which are required by project creation, workspace settings, and connector management tools.

offset.description: Pagination offset (default 0)

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

tool.name: lovable.get_workspace
tool.title: get_workspace
tool.description: Get details for a specific workspace: plan, credit balance, member count, and settings. Use to check available credits before starting work.

tool.name: lovable.list_projects
tool.title: list_projects
tool.description: Search and list projects in a workspace. Supports full-text search by name, AI-generated description, creator name, or email. Uses ngram matching for fuzzy search. Supports filtering by visibility, publish status, folder, and creator.

query.description: Search query. Searches project name, display name, AI-generated description, creator name, and creator email using fuzzy ngram matching. Terms are split on whitespace/underscores/hyphens. All terms must match at least one field.

visibility.description: Filter by visibility: personal (only you), workspace (team), public, or all

user_id.description: Filter by project creator's user ID

viewed_by_me.description: Only return projects viewed by the authenticated user

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response

tool.name: lovable.list_design_systems
tool.title: list_design_systems
tool.description: List design systems available in a workspace. A design system is a reusable Lovable project that ships components, tokens, and styles. Pass any of these IDs as `design_systems` to `create_project` to start a new project from that design system.

tool.name: lovable.list_template_projects
tool.title: list_template_projects
tool.description: List available template projects in a workspace. These can be used as template_project_id when creating a project to clone the template's codebase.

tool.name: lovable.create_project
tool.title: create_project
tool.description: Create a new Lovable project. Pass `workspace_id` and `initial_message`. If `workspace_id` is omitted and exactly one eligible workspace exists, Lovable uses it. If multiple workspaces can create projects, this returns `available_workspaces`; choose one or ask the user, then call create_project again with that `workspace_id`. Returns projectId when creation starts; call render_project_widget with that projectId to show build progress. Projects use Lovable's backend default stack and are full-stack TypeScript apps with Tailwind + shadcn/ui. To start the project from a design system (components, tokens, styles), pass `design_systems` with an ID from `list_design_systems`.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace that can create projects.

initial_message.description: Initial chat message to send after creation

files.description: Uploaded file references to attach to the initial message

file_id.description: Uploaded file ID

type.description: File type

template_project_id.description: Template project ID to clone from (from list_template_projects)

design_systems.description: Design systems to start the project from. Provides components, tokens, and styles. IDs come from list_design_systems. Today only the first entry is applied.

wait.description: Wait for the initial message to be processed. Defaults to true for normal MCP clients.

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait for agent completion (default: 600, max: 600). If it times out, returns status 'in_progress' with the message_id; use get_message to continue polling.

tool.name: lovable.render_project_widget
tool.title: render_project_widget
tool.description: Render the Lovable project status widget for a project that already exists. Call only after create_project returns projectId. Returns widget bootstrap data and does not create or modify projects.

tool.name: lovable.get_project
tool.title: get_project
tool.description: Get details for a specific project. Returns editor_url (Lovable editor) and preview_url (static preview, always available after first prompt). Includes a screenshot of the app when the project status is completed.

tool.name: lovable.set_project_visibility
tool.title: set_project_visibility
tool.description: Set a project's visibility. 'private' makes it editable by workspace members. 'workspace_view' makes it visible (read-only) to workspace members (requires Business plan or higher). 'public' makes it visible to anyone (not available on enterprise plans). 'draft' makes it visible only to the creator (requires Business plan or higher).

tool.name: lovable.set_folder_visibility
tool.title: set_folder_visibility
tool.description: Set a folder's visibility. 'personal' restricts to the creator and collaborators. 'workspace' makes it visible to all workspace members. Changing visibility propagates to all projects in the folder. Nested folders cannot change visibility (move to root first). Personal folders require a Business or Enterprise plan.

tool.name: lovable.move_projects_to_folder
tool.title: move_projects_to_folder
tool.description: Move one or more projects into a workspace folder. Existing folder memberships are removed first. The folder may update project visibility to match folder visibility; the response lists added, skipped, and visibility-updated projects.

project_ids.description: Project IDs to move into the target folder

tool.name: lovable.deploy_project
tool.title: deploy_project
tool.description: Deploy (publish) a project to production hosting on lovable.app. Returns the live URL that anyone can visit.

name.description: Project slug for the published URL

tool.name: lovable.create_variant
tool.title: create_variant
tool.description: Create an independent project variant from the current main branch, or from base_sha when provided. Requires project variants to be enabled for the API key owner or workspace. Create two variants, then call send_message with each variant_id to run alternative implementations in parallel.

label.description: Variant display name. Defaults to the next Draft number.

base_sha.description: Full 40-character commit SHA to base the variant branch on.

tool.name: lovable.send_message
tool.title: send_message
tool.description: Send a chat message to a project's AI agent and wait for the agent to finish. The agent can write and edit code, install npm packages, create pages and components, set up authentication, connect integrations (Stripe, Supabase, etc.), and fix bugs. Write messages in natural language — describe what you want, not how to implement it. Attach images (designs, screenshots) to guide visual changes. Returns the agent's response, activity log, and any edits made. The preview_url is rebuilt once the agent finishes. Set wait=false to return immediately without waiting.

variant_id.description: Variant ID from create_variant. Omit to send the message to the project's main agent.

message.description: Message text for the AI agent

wait.description: Wait for the agent to finish processing (default: true)

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait for agent completion (default: 600, max: 600). If it times out, returns status 'in_progress' with the message_id; use get_message to continue polling.

plan_mode.description: Enable plan mode: the agent discusses and plans without editing code. Use for complex features, architectural decisions, or when you want to align on approach before changes are made (default: false)

file_id.description: Uploaded file ID

type.description: File type

tool.name: lovable.get_message
tool.title: get_message
tool.description: Get the status and content of a message. Pass the message_id and thread_id returned by send_message for thread-aware status. Check the response status field: 'in_progress' means the agent is still working, 'completed' means done.

thread_id.description: Trajectory thread ID returned by send_message

tool.name: lovable.list_messages
tool.title: list_messages
tool.description: List recent messages in a project, newest first. Use this to discover message IDs when you only have a project_id — for example, to fetch the latest assistant response with get_message or look up a diff with get_diff. Paginate older history by passing `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor`.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response

tool.name: lovable.get_workspace_knowledge
tool.title: get_workspace_knowledge
tool.description: Get the workspace's knowledge content. Knowledge is custom instructions that guide the AI agent's behavior across all projects in the workspace.

tool.name: lovable.set_workspace_knowledge
tool.title: set_workspace_knowledge
tool.description: Set the workspace's knowledge content. Knowledge is custom instructions that guide the AI agent's behavior across all projects in the workspace. Max 10,000 characters. Caution: this replaces existing knowledge entirely — read with get_workspace_knowledge first if preserving existing content. Examples of useful knowledge: coding conventions, preferred libraries, brand voice guidelines, API endpoint patterns, or 'always use Supabase for auth'.

content.description: Knowledge content (markdown). Pass empty string to clear.

tool.name: lovable.list_workspace_skills
tool.title: list_workspace_skills
tool.description: List workspace skills. Skills are reusable agent instructions stored in the workspace repo and available to projects in that workspace. Use this before updating or deleting a skill.

include_markdown.description: Include each skill's full SKILL.md contents

tool.name: lovable.get_workspace_skill
tool.title: get_workspace_skill
tool.description: Get a workspace skill, including its full SKILL.md contents. Use this before update_workspace_skill when preserving existing content.

tool.name: lovable.create_workspace_skill
tool.title: create_workspace_skill
tool.description:
Create a workspace skill by adding skills/{skill_name}/SKILL.md to the workspace repo. Only workspace admins and owners can create skills. The markdown must include valid frontmatter with matching name and a description, for example: ---
name: my-skill
description: What this skill helps with
---

# My Skill
...

skill_name.description: Skill name; must match the frontmatter name

tool.name: lovable.update_workspace_skill
tool.title: update_workspace_skill
tool.description: Update a workspace skill by replacing skills/{skill_name}/SKILL.md in the workspace repo. Only workspace admins and owners can update skills. Read the existing skill first with get_workspace_skill if you need to preserve content.

skill_name.description: Skill name; must match the frontmatter name

markdown.description: Full replacement SKILL.md contents, including frontmatter

tool.name: lovable.delete_workspace_skill
tool.title: delete_workspace_skill
tool.description: Delete a workspace skill from the workspace repo. Only workspace admins and owners can delete skills. This removes the skill directory and cannot be undone except by recreating the skill.

tool.name: lovable.list_project_skills
tool.title: list_project_skills
tool.description: List skills present in the project repo, including whether each skill is currently enabled for agent runs in this project. Use this before enabling or disabling a project skill.

tool.name: lovable.enable_project_skill
tool.title: enable_project_skill
tool.description: Enable a project skill so the Lovable agent uses it for this project's agent runs.

tool.name: lovable.disable_project_skill
tool.title: disable_project_skill
tool.description: Disable a project skill without removing it from the project repo, so the Lovable agent stops using it for this project's agent runs.

tool.name: lovable.get_project_knowledge
tool.title: get_project_knowledge
tool.description: Get a project's knowledge content. Knowledge is custom instructions that guide the AI agent's behavior for this specific project.

tool.name: lovable.set_project_knowledge
tool.title: set_project_knowledge
tool.description: Set a project's knowledge content. Knowledge is custom instructions that guide the AI agent's behavior for this specific project. Max 10,000 characters. Caution: this replaces existing knowledge entirely — read with get_project_knowledge first if preserving existing content. Examples of useful knowledge: coding conventions, preferred libraries, brand voice guidelines, API endpoint patterns, or 'always use Supabase for auth'.

content.description: Knowledge content (markdown). Pass empty string to clear.

tool.name: lovable.get_diff
tool.title: get_diff
tool.description: Get the code diff from a message or commit. Pass message_id (from send_message) to see what the agent changed, or sha for a specific commit. Returns a unified diff.

message_id.description: Message ID (from send_message) — resolves the diff from the message's edit

sha.description: Commit SHA to diff (alternative to message_id)

base_sha.description: Base commit SHA for comparison (defaults to parent commit)

tool.name: lovable.list_files
tool.title: list_files
tool.description: List a page of files in a Lovable project. Optionally pass latest_commit_sha from get_project, or commit_sha from send_message/list_edits. Use pagination.next_cursor to fetch more pages.

ref.description: Git ref — commit SHA, branch name, or tag

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous page

tool.name: lovable.read_file
tool.title: read_file
tool.description: Read the contents of a single file in a Lovable project. Optionally pass latest_commit_sha from get_project, or commit_sha from send_message/list_edits. Returns the raw file content as text.

ref.description: Git ref — commit SHA, branch name, or tag

tool.name: lovable.list_edits
tool.title: list_edits
tool.description: List the edit history of a Lovable project. Each edit represents a code change with a commit_sha that can be used with get_diff. Supports pagination via the before parameter (use created_at from the last edit).

before.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for pagination (created_at of last edit in previous page)

tool.name: lovable.get_file_upload_url
tool.title: get_file_upload_url
tool.description: Get a presigned URL to upload a file. Workflow: 1) call this to get upload_url and file_id, 2) PUT the file content to the upload_url, 3) pass the file_id in the files array of send_message or create_project.

tool.name: lovable.get_database_status
tool.title: get_database_status
tool.description: Check whether a cloud database (PostgreSQL via Supabase) is enabled for a project. Call this first before querying or connecting — if not enabled, use enable_database to provision it.

tool.name: lovable.enable_database
tool.title: enable_database
tool.description: Provision a cloud PostgreSQL database (Supabase) for a project. This operation takes 30-60 seconds. Only needed once — after enabling, the database persists. Returns the database status once provisioning completes.

tool.name: lovable.query_database
tool.title: query_database
tool.description: Execute a SQL query against a project's cloud PostgreSQL database. Returns rows as JSON objects. Supports SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and DDL statements. The database must be enabled first (use get_database_status to check, then enable_database if needed). Caution: write operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP) modify production data permanently — prefer SELECT for inspection unless a write is explicitly required.

tool.name: lovable.list_connectors
tool.title: list_connectors
tool.description: List all connectors (integrations) available in a workspace. Connectors give the AI agent access to external services like Stripe, Supabase, Shopify, Slack, and more. Grouped by type: standard (OAuth-based API connectors), seamless (zero-config integrations), and MCP (Model Context Protocol servers). Each includes its enabled/disabled status. See https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/introduction for details.

tool.name: lovable.list_connections
tool.title: list_connections
tool.description: List authenticated connections (accounts) for connectors in a workspace. Shows which specific accounts are connected — for example, which Google Drive account or Stripe account is linked. Use list_connectors to see available connector types, then list_connections to see which ones have active connections. Optionally filter by connector_id.

connector_id.description: Filter by connector ID (e.g. 'google_drive', 'stripe'). Omit to list all connections.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

tool.name: lovable.list_custom_connectors
tool.title: list_custom_connectors
tool.description: List connectors that have been added to a workspace (both from the catalog and custom). These are the connectors the AI agent can use during chat. To add a new one, call add_connector to get the dashboard URL the user should open. Use remove_connector to remove.

tool.name: lovable.add_connector
tool.title: add_connector
tool.description: Get the Lovable dashboard URL where the user can add a connector. Connectors must always be added through the dashboard — the MCP cannot add them programmatically. Use this tool to return the deep link the user should open.

connector_id.description: Catalog connector ID (e.g. 'linear', 'notion'). Optional — omit for the general connectors page.

tool.name: lovable.remove_connector
tool.title: remove_connector
tool.description: Remove a connector from a workspace.

tool.name: lovable.list_available_connectors
tool.title: list_available_connectors
tool.description: Browse available connector templates. Returns connector IDs that can be passed to add_connector.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

tool.name: lovable.remix_project
tool.title: remix_project
tool.description: Remix (fork) an existing project into a workspace. Creates a copy of the source project. Waits for the remix to complete and returns the new project details.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace ID for the new project

include_history.description: Copy chat history to the new project

include_custom_knowledge.description: Copy custom knowledge (instructions) to the new project

project_name.description: Custom name for the new project

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait for remix completion (default: 600, max: 600).

tool.name: lovable.get_project_analytics
tool.title: get_project_analytics
tool.description: Get historical analytics for a published project: visitors, pageviews, bounce rate, session duration, and breakdowns by page, source, device, and country.

tool.name: lovable.get_project_analytics_trend
tool.title: get_project_analytics_trend
tool.description: Get real-time visitor trend for a published project. Returns the current visitor count and visit counts in 5-minute intervals over the last 30 minutes.
